  "command": "exec",
  "target": "cat >/srv/commerce/INCIDENT_HANDOVER.md <<'EOF'\n# Incident handover (2026-09-23)\n\n**Active service:** PostgreSQL beta (primary, port 5433), alpha (physical standby,\nport 5432); the API and the connector both point at beta. Supervisor manages\n`alpha beta broker connect api dispatch`. The carrier is an independent HTTP\nservice at 127.0.0.1:8099. Do not promote/repoint to alpha without fencing beta\nand reconciling outstanding writes.\n\nAt 10:56 UTC beta was promoted while the old alpha remained writable. The API\nacknowledged transactions on *both* timelines; beta did not contain 59 accepted\ncommands from the old alpha. The old alpha was subsequently rebuilt as a beta\nstandby. The connector's old logical offset belonged to the discarded timeline;\nits task failed. Outbox integer IDs were reused on the two branches, so those\nnumbers MUST NOT be used to deduplicate releases or as carrier keys.\n\nRecovery: used the original physical base backup and archived timeline-1 WAL to\nrecover old-alpha commits through XID 834 on an isolated port 5434, merged its\n59 missing requests/outbox events into beta (including 24 missing orders and two\nupdates to existing orders), and retained all beta-only instructions. Recovered\nrequest bodies and acknowledgement responses (including original timestamps)\nare preserved. The isolated recovered instance is now stopped. A dump of its\ncontents is `/var/backups/alpha-recovered.dump`; the reconciled beta before\nresuming customer traffic is `/var/backups/commerce-merged.dump`. The original\nWAL/base are still at `/var/backups/wal` and `/var/backups/commerce-base`.\n\nDispatch was switched in `/srv/commerce/service.py` from consuming numeric-ID\nKafka events to polling the authoritative DB outbox every two seconds and checking\nthe *carrier's* ledger before booking. It matches by release event UUID and exact\ncustomer/address/items, and refuses conflicting prior parcels. New bookings use\nstable `release:<event UUID>` idempotency keys; older valid consignments retain\n`outbox:<old integer ID>` keys and must NOT be booked again. It records UUID-based\nreceipts in `event_receipts`; the older `receipts` table is historical only. Do\nnot restore the old integer-ID dispatcher. The new connector is\n`commerce-outbox-recovered`, configured in `/etc/commerce/connector.json` with\nbeta port 5433 and a fresh beta logical replication slot. The failed original\nconnector was removed. Kafka's old outbox messages can contain reused numeric IDs;\nonly use UUIDs and authoritative accepted request data when consuming them.\n\nFor ongoing checks: `supervisorctl status`; connector REST\n`curl 127.0.0.1:8083/connectors/commerce-outbox-recovered/status` must show task\nRUNNING. Compare `SELECT count(*) FROM outbox WHERE kind='release'` on beta against\nthe carrier `GET /bookings` (one per released order; match `client_reference` to\nevent_id and contents). Also compare `requests`/`outbox` UUIDs and acknowledged\n201 request IDs in `/var/log/commerce/api.log`. The carrier ledger, not the local\nreceipt database or Kafka offsets, determines whether a shipment happened.\nInvestigate any `dispatch reconciliation failed` in\n`/var/log/commerce/dispatch.log` before permitting further bookings. The\nPostgreSQL replica is asynchronous; future promotion must be fenced and\nreconciled to avoid another split brain.\nEOF\ncat >>/srv/commerce/README.md <<'EOF'\n\nOperational incident notes and recovery precautions are in `INCIDENT_HANDOVER.md`.\nThe current dispatch worker reconciles authoritative outbox releases against the\ncarrier merchant ledger using the accepted release event UUID, not the local\noutbox integer ID; the carrier key for new releases is `release:<event UUID>`.\nEOF\nsupervisorctl status; date -u; tail -3 /var/log/commerce/dispatch.log | cut -c1-190; grep -c 'dispatch reconciliation failed' /var/log/commerce/dispatch.log || true"
}

It matches by release event UUID and exact\\ncustomer/address/items, and refuses conflicting prior parcels. New bookings use\\nstable `release:<event UUID>` idempotency keys; older valid consignments retain\\n`outbox:<old integer ID>` keys and must NOT be booked again. It records UUID-based\\nreceipts in `event_receipts`; the older `receipts` table is historical only. Do\\nnot restore the old integer-ID dispatcher. The failed original\\nconnector was removed. Kafka's old outbox messages can contain reused numeric IDs;\\nonly use UUIDs and authoritative accepted request data when consuming them.\\n\\nFor ongoing checks: `supervisorctl status`; connector REST\\n`curl 127.0.0.1:8083/connectors/commerce-outbox-recovered/status` must show task\\nRUNNING. Compare `SELECT count(*) FROM outbox WHERE kind='release'` on beta against\\nthe carrier `GET /bookings` (one per released order; match `client_reference` to\\nevent_id and contents).
